topicName: CI/CD for Data Pipelines and Infrastructure as Code (Terraform)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"CI/CD for Data Pipelines and Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) in ETL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern data engineering requires robust automation not only for the Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) application logic but also for the underlying infrastructure that supports it. Combining Terraform for Infrastructure as Code (IaC) with Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines ensures reproducible environments, automated testing, and seamless deployments."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Architectural Overview"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this architecture, we separate our repository into two main components: infrastructure definitions (Terraform modules for data lakes, warehouses, and orchestration engines) and ETL application code (Python scripts, SQL models, or dbt projects). The CI/CD pipeline validates, tests, and deploys both components sequentially."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Defining Infrastructure with Terraform"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"We begin by writing Terraform configurations to provision our data platform. Below is a sample configuration creating an AWS S3 bucket for raw ETL data and a Snowflake database for transformation."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"resource "aws_s3_bucket" "raw_zone" {
  bucket = "company-etl-raw-zone-prod"
  force_destroy = true
}

resource "snowflake_database" "etl_db" {
  name    = "PROD_ETL_DB"
  comment = "Database for automated ETL pipelines"
}"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Designing the CI/CD Pipeline"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"A complete CI/CD pipeline for data platforms typically follows these stages:"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Linting and Static Analysis: Check Terraform syntax using tflint and Python code using flake8."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Unit Testing: Run pytest for custom ETL transformations."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Infrastructure Plan: Execute terraform plan to preview changes."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Deployment: Apply infrastructure changes and deploy updated ETL scripts."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Implementing GitHub Actions Workflow"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is an example GitHub Actions workflow configuration that automates both Terraform provisioning and ETL validation."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"name: "ETL CI/CD Pipeline"

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "main" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "main" ]

jobs:
  terraform:
    name: "Terraform Deploy"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2

      - name: Terraform Init
        run: terraform init

      - name: Terraform Plan
        run: terraform plan -input=false

      - name: Terraform Apply
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
        run: terraform apply -auto-approve -input=false"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Best Practices for Data CI/CD"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always use remote state storage (e.g., AWS S3 with DynamoDB locking) for Terraform to prevent concurrency issues in team environments."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Separate state files or workspaces for staging and production environments."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Incorporate data contract testing and schema validation tests before promoting ETL pipelines to production."}]
